exponential_growth.name: Exponential Growth
exponential_growth.description: A single positive feedback loop. More leads to more.
explanation: Structure: One stock (Population), one flow (Births), one positive feedback loop.
| Births |---->| Pop.  |
The population produces births. Births increase the population.
More population means more births means more population.
This is the engine behind compound interest, viral spread,
and the early phase of any growth story.
The signature: a curve that bends upward, accelerating forever.
Nothing in nature does this for long.

logistic_growth.name: Logistic Growth
logistic_growth.description: Growth meets its limit. Positive loop vs. negative loop.
explanation: Structure: One stock, two competing feedback loops.
| Growth |           | Crowding |
|     v       v     |
At low population, the positive loop dominates: growth accelerates.
As population approaches carrying capacity, the negative loop
strengthens: resources thin, growth rate drops.
The signature: an S-curve. Fast growth, then a plateau.
This is the shape of learning, market saturation, healing.

oscillation.name: Predator-Prey Oscillation
oscillation.description: Two species locked in a dance. Negative feedback creates cycles.
explanation: Structure: Two stocks, two interlinked negative feedback loops.
|  Prey   |---------->| Predators|
More prey feeds predator growth. More predators kill prey.
As prey decline, predators starve. As predators decline, prey recover.
The system chases its own tail forever.
The signature: two waves, offset in time.
Prey peak first, predators follow, then both crash, then repeat.
This is the Lotka-Volterra dynamic -- found in ecosystems,
inventory cycles, and boom-bust economies.

overshoot.name: Overshoot and Collapse
overshoot.description: Growth overshoots capacity because of delay. Then the fall.
explanation: Structure: Positive growth loop, negative resource loop, with DELAY.
| Growth |           | Resource |
| Loop   |           | Depletion|
|     v       v     |
+----| Pop.    |----+     <--- delay here
v
|Resources|
Population grows, consuming resources. But the signal that
resources are running low takes time to affect birth rates.
By the time the system 'notices,' it has already overshot.
Resources collapse. Population follows.
The signature: growth, overshoot, crash.
This is the shape of bubbles, ecological collapse,
and any system where feedback arrives too late.

s_curve.name: S-Curve Adoption
s_curve.description: How ideas spread: word of mouth meets saturation.
explanation: Structure: Adoption driven by contact between adopters and non-adopters.
| Potential   |-------->| Adopters |
| Adopters    |  adopt  |          |
adoption_rate = adopters * potential * contact_rate
Early on: few adopters, slow spread (nobody to hear about it).
Middle: many adopters AND many potential -- fastest growth.
Late: few potential left -- growth slows, market saturates.
The signature: slow start, explosive middle, gradual plateau.
This is the Bass diffusion model -- the shape of every technology,
every fashion trend, every idea that catches on.

flows.adoption: adopters * potential * contact_rate / total_population + potential * innovation_rate
